summary: Round 7 (Seyi's round-6 re-review, CHANGES_REQUIRED): rebuilds the BIO-IDN-006-QA-08 interim mitigation to match ADR-0006 (docs/adr/ADR-0006-actor-identity-and-authorization-boundary.md) Decision 3's authoritative text exactly, superseding round 6's OperatorKeyGate. Root cause, confirmed directly by god via git merge-base --is-ancestor: feature/BIO-IDN-006 branched off develop BEFORE ADR-0006 was committed there, so the ADR file had literally never existed in this worktree - neither I nor any reviewer of this branch could have read Decision 3's actual text before this round. God's earlier round-4/round-6 direction (a simple shared X-Operator-Key secret, checked directly) was her own imprecise paraphrase of Kemi's architectural ruling, sent before Kemi refined it into ADR-0006's committed text; Seyi's round-6 FAIL correctly re-flagged the resulting gate as still too coarse (a secret holder could assert ANY person id via X-Actor-Id with zero binding between the shared secret and the specific identity claimed). God merged develop into this branch (commit ac58710, clean, no conflicts - my only local uncommitted file, Zainab's own evidence artifact, was left untouched), making ADR-0006 visible and citable for the first time. Decision 3's actual mechanism: 'X-Actor-Id may remain the transport, but only if a trusted edge strips any caller-supplied value and injects a verified one, and the application checks that injected value's provenance before trusting it for an authorization decision - never accepting a caller-supplied value directly.' This story implements only the application-side half (verifying provenance of the actor id ActorResolver already resolved, before any authorization decision uses it) - the trusted edge itself (stripping/injecting the verified value) is explicitly Emeka's infrastructure concern per the ADR, outside this story's surface. Documented assumption for the interim, no-edge-yet state (stated explicitly per god's request): an operator/deployment script computes the same HMAC-SHA256 proof out of band using the shared Rbac:ActorProvenanceSecret and attaches it as X-Actor-Provenance, modelling exactly what the edge will eventually automate.
notes: Fix: replaced OperatorKeyGate (a bare shared secret, checked independently of which actor id was asserted) with ActorProvenanceGate - an HMAC-SHA256 proof of the SPECIFIC actor id ActorResolver already resolved, keyed by a shared provenance secret (IActorProvenanceStore/HmacActorProvenanceStore/ActorProvenanceProvisioning), checked immediately after actor resolution and strictly before any authorization decision uses the value, on the same four surfaces as before (role assign/revoke, permission-grant configuration, sensitive-action-rule configuration, maker-checker request/decide). The real difference from the retired gate: the proof is cryptographically bound to the exact identity being asserted in this request (a proof computed for one actor id does not satisfy a request asserting a different one), not an independent flag that waves any request through regardless of which actor id it names. Provisioning still mirrors BIO-CRD-001-QA-01's ITenantCredentialStore precedent: constant-time comparison via CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals, IConfiguration-loaded Rbac:ActorProvenanceSecret out of band, never reachable via HTTP, fails closed when unconfigured (an unconfigured store computes HMAC with a fixed dummy key no legitimate caller could ever match, so it fails closed without a separate branch or timing side-channel). Documented explicitly, in the class's own header comment and the README, against ADR-0006 Decision 3's own 'what this interim closure explicitly does not buy' language - the residual (a secret holder can still compute a valid proof for any actor id, including self-approving maker-checker via two different ids across two calls) is identical in kind to round 6's residual and remains accepted and disclosed per Decision 3, not something this round tries to close. Verified end-to-end: dotnet build clean (0 errors). 113/113 feature-local tests (test fixture helpers rewritten to compute a real HMAC proof per asserted actor id rather than presenting a static secret; new tests proving a wrong-actor-id-bound proof is rejected identically to a missing one, and that the provenance gate runs before authorization so an attacker learns nothing about actor authority). 86/86 integration tests (RbacHostChannelTests.cs rewritten the same way; one known non-deterministic ObservabilityTests flake hit mid-run, isolated rerun 9/9 clean and full rerun 86/86 clean, documented since BIO-IDN-004). 121/121 offline structural checks (9 QA-08 checks rewritten/added, including one confirming ADR-0006 itself exists and names Decision 3, and one confirming the gate is checked on the SAME already-resolved actor id immediately after ActorResolver runs). Full scripts/quality.sh (repo-wide gate): QUALITY PASS, 0 failures; contract-freeze PASS (39 artifacts - up from 38, confirming ADR-0006 is now counted; 83 future stories); traceability PASS (19 implemented stories); module-reference-direction PASS; secret-scan clean.
